response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack software engineer (14+ years) with strong web, backend, and some low-latency systems work, but the resume shows essentially no overlap with the core requirements of this Principal Performance Architect role: no SoC/IP modeling, no hardware architecture or hardware-software co-design, no AI accelerator, GPU, SIMD/MIMD, or deep-learning workload optimization experience. The only adjacent items are brief C/C++ work at National Instruments and embedded/robotics exposure at Altom, which fall far short of principal-level silicon performance architecture. Education is a BS in Computer Science with sufficient years of experience to meet the formal bar, but the domain expertise gap is decisive.
strengths: 14+ years of broad software engineering experience, including staff-level roles
Low-latency, high-throughput systems work (D, async I/O, fibers, millions of req/s)
Some C/C++ and embedded/robotics exposure plus strong OSS and teaching record
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling or hardware architecture experience whatsoever
No AI accelerator, GPU, SIMD/MIMD, or DNN training/inference optimization background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack, not silicon performance architecture at principal level

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware co-design
No AI accelerator / GPU / deep-learning workload expertise
Extensive senior software engineering and performance-sensitive systems work
